provider.name: Wikispecies
provider.organization_type: collaborative multilingual taxonomic directory, nomenclature, author, publication, institution, type-locality, reference, API, dump, and Wikimedia integration infrastructure
provider.description: Wikispecies is a Wikimedia project focused on taxonomy and nomenclature. It provides collaboratively maintained pages for taxa, taxonomic authors, publications, institutions, type localities, references, taxonavigation, synonyms, nomenclatural notes, external identifiers, and links to Wikidata, Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, and specialist taxonomic authorities.
institutional_context: Wikidata, Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, MediaWiki, Toolforge, and external nomenclatural and taxonomic authorities

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting Wikispecies documentation, organization, governance, taxon pages, taxonavigation, scientific names, authorship, nomenclatural status, synonyms, types, authors, publications, institutions, type localities, references, templates, categories, APIs, dumps, recent-change streams, bot workflows, quality control, licenses, software, standards, nomenclatural codes, and related authorities.
purpose.authoritative_notice: Wikispecies is a community-edited secondary taxonomic directory and is not itself an official nomenclatural registry. The relevant nomenclatural code, original publication, official registry, type repository, specialist taxonomic authority, Wikimedia policy, page revision history, API documentation, dump manifest, and cited source remain authoritative for names, acts, types, identifiers, versions, rights, and provenance.

notes: Verify current Action API modules, REST routes, response schemas, authentication, maxlag, throttling, and deprecations.
Verify current Wikispecies dump file names, compression formats, checksums, completion markers, and retention.
Do not infer undocumented administrative or write endpoints from browser traffic.
Do not store passwords, bot passwords, OAuth secrets, cookies, CSRF tokens, private account data, or session identifiers.
Capture exact current Wikispecies, Wikimedia Foundation, Commons, software, API, and dump legal wording.
Separate page text, revision history, Commons media, Wikidata structured data, external taxonomic databases, publications, and software.
Preserve page title, page ID, revision ID, contributors, license version, source URL, access date, dump date, checksum, and provenance.
Wikispecies taxonomic facts and nomenclatural acts must be traced to original publications and official registries; linked source text and media may have separate rights.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Wikispecies routes, policies, templates, API modules, REST endpoints, dump file names, nomenclatural guidance, and legal wording may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.

Do not recursively crawl every taxon, author, publication, institution, category member, template transclusion, revision, API result, EventStream event, or dump member when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store passwords, bot passwords, OAuth secrets, cookies, CSRF tokens, private account data, or session identifiers.
Wikispecies page text, revision history, Commons media, Wikidata structured data, external taxonomic sources, publications, API output, dumps, and software may carry different rights.
Wikispecies is not an official nomenclatural registry. Preserve and prioritize original publications, nomenclatural codes, type repositories, and specialist taxonomic authorities.

Always preserve page title, page ID, revision ID, timestamp, scientific name, authorship, rank, parent taxon, accepted name, synonyms, nomenclatural status, types and repositories, protologue and references, author and institution identifiers, external taxonomic identifiers, source URL, access date, dump date and checksum, license, attribution, and provenance.
